In the descriptions of power ups and weapons on the hull full screen the descriptions should be given two lines

---

## Plan clarifications (plan skill, downtime run)

**Goal (user story):** As a player who fills the mineral hold, I want each power-up/weapon description in the hold-full choice to have room for **two lines** of text, so longer descriptions stay readable and on-screen instead of running past the edge of the 960 x 540 playfield.

**Terminology clarification — "hull full screen".** Read as the **hold-full choice overlay** (`src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`, heading `HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP`) — the ship's (cargo) hold filling up. It is the only full-screen surface that renders power-up/weapon descriptions beneath each option; the gym help overlay already word-wraps its descriptions (`src/scenes/HelpScene.ts`), while `MineralChoiceScene` currently renders each description as a **single unwrapped** Phaser text (13 px monospace, no `wordWrap`).

**Current behaviour (evidence).** Row layout is a fixed three-line block: name at `y`, description at `y + 28`, detail (change summary / `★ New`) at `y + 48`, row pitch 84 px (`CHOICE_ROW_PITCH`). The longest power-up description is 210 characters (Teleport) and the longest weapon description 107 characters (Arc); at 13 px monospace an unwrapped line is wider than the 960 px playfield, so long descriptions visibly overflow today.

**Assumption (documented, non-blocking).** "Two lines" means the description **area** must accommodate up to two wrapped lines (layout capacity), not that the shared catalogue copy is rewritten to be exactly two lines. This follows the title's "to allow for more content" and keeps the catalogue copy (and gym-help parity) unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Two-line description area.** Each option's description renders with `wordWrap` constrained to a readable width and `maxLines: 2`, so descriptions up to two lines display fully inside the 960 x 540 playfield.
- **AC2 — No overlap / no regression.** Name -> description (one or two lines) -> change summary / `★ New` remain a non-overlapping vertical block, and consecutive option rows never collide — verified by a scene test that asserts rendered bounds.
- **AC3 — Overflow safety.** A description longer than two lines is truncated to two lines (ellipsis or clipping) and never overflows the playfield horizontally.
- **AC4 — Backward-compatible contracts.** One-line descriptions still render as one line; an option with no description still renders no description line; `getOptionLabels()`, `getDescriptionLines()` and `getDetailLines()` keep their existing contracts.
- **AC5 — Single source of copy.** Descriptions stay resolved from the shared catalogue via `getHelpDescription` (`src/utils/gymHelp.ts`) — no copy duplicated in the scene.
- **AC6 — Gym-game parity.** `PlayScene` and every gym share `MineralChoiceScene`; no divergent render path or second overlay is introduced.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Scene tests cover: two-line wrapping of a long description, truncation/overflow safety, the one-line and no-description fallbacks, and non-overlapping row geometry.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** GDD §4.4.1 and the README entries for `MineralChoiceScene` / the hold-full overlay are updated from "one-line description" to a two-line description area; the docs guard (`src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts`) still passes.
- **AC9 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the change (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — description `wordWrap` width and `maxLines: 2`, plus dynamic vertical offsets / row pitch so a two-line description never collides with the detail line or the next option.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — wrap, truncation, fallback and layout tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4.1) and `README.md` — copy updates.
- `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` — docs guard (extend if its wording assertion requires it).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Which screen is "the hull full screen"?** Not asked interactively (downtime run with no producer present). Resolved by repository research: the phrase matches the hold-full choice overlay (the ship's hold, heading "HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP", `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`), the only full-screen surface that shows power-up/weapon descriptions without wrapping. Evidence: `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (description rendered at 13 px with no `wordWrap`), `src/scenes/HelpScene.ts` (gym help already wraps), GDD §4.4.1 "Hold full → power-up choice".
- **Q2 — Should the catalogue copy itself be lengthened to use both lines?** **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, producer):** this plan allocates a two-line area only and leaves the shared catalogue wording unchanged, preserving gym-help parity. If the producer prefers the copy itself to be extended, that is a follow-up item where the catalogue (`src/powerups/types.ts`, `src/utils/weapons.ts`) and the gym help would change together.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 — plan skill (downtime run) after effort/risk pre-check `skip` (Extra Small / Low): appended goal, terminology clarification, current-behaviour evidence, documented assumption, 9 ACs, Key Files and the question Appendix; recorded the six review-stage notes and the AC coverage review in comments; effort/risk re-estimated (Extra Small / Low, ~1.1 h expected). No child work items created (single deliverable increment).

## Goal (tracer-bullet vertical slice)

Ship the first end-to-end music slice: the menu/attract ambient track ("Star Drift", Lydian) played through the existing shared AudioContext, driven by a minimal music state machine, with the autoplay/gesture guard and an independent music volume control.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.
- [ ] Music volume and mute are independent of SFX and persisted in the settings record.
- [ ] The state machine enters and leaves the menu/attract state only at a bar boundary of the shared beat clock.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stem looping, the gesture guard, independent volume routing and the menu/attract transition; all playback degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext.

- [ ] Covers parent AC5: **Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.

## Minimal implementation

1. Bake the "Star Drift" ambient stem via the ToneForge pipeline and add it to the cue/stem manifest (smallest slice of the stem pipeline).
2. Add src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (facade) and a minimal src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts with the menu/attract state.
3. Wire gesture-driven start/resume through MenuScene using the shared AudioContext.
4. Extend SettingsRecord with musicVolume/musicMuted and route them independently of SFX.
5. Add unit tests for each acceptance criterion.

- Blocked by Music contract mapping and traceability guard (AH-0MVMH2OPY001X6M3), which is itself blocked by the chapter docs item (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W).
- Reuses the shared AudioContext and provider seam in src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts.

## Risky assumption

Baked stems (not runtime synthesis) are the delivery mechanism, consistent with the shipped ToneForge pipeline; recorded as an assumption in the parent item's plan.

**Key Files:**
- src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (new)
- src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts (new)

# Intake Brief — Mini Boss explosions

**Work item:** AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z (feature, high)
**Headline:** On mini-boss defeat, explode every remaining wave-gating enemy
(escorts plus the mini-boss's live minions) in a staggered sweep, add
`max(0, 30 − n)` extra explosions scattered at random across the scene plus 10
around the mini-boss's death point, and hold the mini-boss reward overlay until
every explosion animation has finished.

**Source request (verbatim):** "When the mini-boss it defeated all remaining
enemies should explode, add an additional 30 - # of enemies explosions
scattered randomly across the scene and 10 around the mini-boss. Do not show
the reward screen until all explosions have completed their animation."

## Problem statement

Defeating a mini-boss currently destroys only the mini-boss body (with its own
boss-scale explosion): surviving escorts and summoned minions stay on the field,
no celebration scatter fires, and the reward overlay opens on the same frame as
the kill — mid-explosion — so the defeat reads as abrupt rather than
celebratory. The operator wants a cascading explosion sweep on the defeat frame,
a short celebratory scatter, and the reward screen held back until the last
burst has finished animating.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, when I defeat the mini-boss I want every remaining
  enemy to blow up and an extra barrage of explosions across the screen, so the
  kill feels like a clear victory moment."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want the reward screen to appear only after the
  explosion display has finished, so I don't miss the celebration."
- **Developer/tester (gym)** — "As a tester I want the mini-boss gym's EXPLODE
  button to show the same sweep, so what I verify in the gym is what ships."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Remaining wave-gating enemies explode.** On the mini-boss's lethal
  hit, every live wave-gating enemy is destroyed in a staggered explosion sweep
  that begins on the defeat frame. Scope is **escort ships plus the mini-boss's
  live summoned minions**; non-blocking hazards (`asteroid`, `lane-traffic`, per
  `isNonBlockingHazard`) are **not** swept and remain on the field.
- **AC2 — Extra scattered explosions.** The sweep adds `max(0, 30 − n)` extra
  particle explosions, where `n` is the number of wave-gating enemies swept
  (escorts + minions), placed at positions sampled uniformly at random across
  the playfield, plus exactly **10** explosions clustered around the mini-boss's
  death position captured at destruction (see AC9 for the additional finale
  cluster added after producer review). Edge cases are explicit: `n = 0` → 30
  extras; `n = 30` → 0 extras; `n > 30` → 0 extras (never negative, never an
  exception). Total scattered bursts therefore never exceed 30.
- **AC3 — Reward screen waits for the explosions.** The mini-boss reward overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`, opened by `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`) opens only
  after the last explosion burst in the sweep has completed its animation. The
  `miniBossRewardOpen` latch still opens exactly one overlay per defeat, and the
  demo auto-select contract (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F) still applies after the delay
  (attract mode never stalls).
- **AC4 — Cosmetic-only destruction.** Swept enemies are removed from play but
  award **no score**, drop **no minerals / power-ups / Extra Life**, and emit
  **no kill telemetry**. Wave/level accounting still clears exactly once,
  **after** the sweep: the level advance never fires mid-display and never fires
  twice.
- **AC5 — Game↔gym parity.** `GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE path runs the **same**
  shared sweep helper as `PlayScene` (one implementation consumed by both); the
  repo duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the
  gym-parity docs assertion pass.
- **AC6 — Determinism and meaningful tests.** All random placement/jitter uses
  the run-seeded RNG (no `Math.random()` in the sweep), so a seed replays the
  same display; unit tests cover the count formula at the edges (`n = 0, 1, 29,
  30, 40`), the minion/hazard scope split, and the sweep-completion → overlay
  ordering (overlay does not open before the last burst finishes).
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries**
  (notably GDD §3.3/§4.4.4 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

- **AC9 — Mini-boss finale (producer review, 2026-10-29).** On the defeat frame
  the mini-boss additionally receives **20 finale bursts** clustered **in and
  around** its captured death position — 10 anchored bursts (`AC2`) are kept
  and the finale adds a wider, denser cluster on top. The finale fires **in
  pairs: two bursts every 0.25 s** (ten pairs), starting after the anchored
  celebration so the display builds to the mini-boss's biggest beat. The
  finale is run-seeded (no `Math.random()`), awards nothing (AC4), and the
  reward overlay (AC3) waits for the last finale pair to finish animating.
  Total sweep bursts are therefore bounded at
  `n + max(0, 30 − n) + 10 + 20 ≤ 60`.

## Constraints

- **Shared-code parity:** the sweep lives once in a new shared module under
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss` — no
  divergent copy (AGENTS.md "Game Architecture Conventions").
- **Reuse the existing VFX:** explosions go through
  `spawnExplosionParticles` (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) — same particle
  system, ~400 ms burst lifespan, shared per-kind VFX registry
  (`getExplosionVfxCounts`). No new particle system.
- **No reward of any kind** for swept kills (operator answer Q2 = B + C): this
  is celebration VFX only, so the mini-boss reward remains the single reward
  for the encounter.
- **Ordering:** the reward overlay's `setPaused(true)` would freeze the tween
  animations, so the sweep must be allowed to run and complete before the
  overlay pauses the scene.
- **Minion capture order:** mini-boss minions are owned by the `MiniBoss` entity
  and are currently torn down by `MiniBoss.destroy()` → `_clearMinions()`
  (plain `destroy(true)`, no explosion). The sweep must capture the live minions
  (e.g. `miniBoss.getMinions()`) **before** `miniBoss.destroy()`, otherwise they
  cannot be exploded or counted in `n`.
- **Demo mode** must remain non-blocking: the delayed overlay keeps the existing
  auto-select behaviour.
- **Determinism:** seeded RNG for placement/jitter, per the repo VFX contract.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` (~L2920): on the lethal hit captures a
  `MiniBossDefeatContext`, calls `miniBoss.destroy()` (which also clears
  minions), fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` (checkpoint + reward), then replays
  one destruction through the wave state machine with a stale-count
  reconciliation guard.
- `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` calls `openMiniBossReward` **synchronously** → the
  overlay launches and `setPaused(true)` runs on the defeat frame.
- Remaining escorts/survivors are not destroyed; minions are silently torn down
  with the boss body. Hazards (`isNonBlockingHazard`) are never wave-accounted.
- `MiniBoss extends Boss`; its own death already plays a boss-scale explosion.
  `BaseEnemy.destroySelf(scale?)` / `playExplosion(scale)` is the shared
  per-enemy explosion seam, and `destroySelf()` marks the entity dead without
  awarding anything — so a cosmetic sweep can reuse it directly.
- `GymMiniBoss` destroys via EXPLODE → `MiniBoss.takeDamage()` →
  `destroySelf()`; it has no reward overlay, so the gym shows the sweep only.
- Kill accounting lives in `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` (score → drops → wave
  advance); the sweep must **not** call that path (AC4).

## Desired change

Introduce a shared `miniBossDeathSweep` helper (pure planner + thin Phaser
executor) that:

1. collects the sweep targets — live wave-gating enemies (excluding
   `isNonBlockingHazard`) plus the mini-boss's live minions captured before the
   entity is destroyed;
2. staggers their `destroySelf()` explosions over a short window so the sweep
   reads as a cascade (a modest burst scale — enemy-scale, not boss-scale);
3. spawns the `max(0, 30 − n)` random scattered extras plus 10 bursts anchored
   at the mini-boss death position, all drawn through
   `spawnExplosionParticles` with the run-seeded RNG;
4. reports completion (last burst finished) so `PlayScene` then opens the
   mini-boss reward overlay; wave accounting advances once, after the sweep.

`GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE button calls the same helper (tests observe the burst
counts and completion).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — **new** shared sweep planner
  (count/placement maths) + Phaser executor + completion callback, with tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageMiniBoss` (capture minions before
  `destroy()`), `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` / `openMiniBossReward` (defer the
  overlay until sweep completion), single deferred wave advance.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — EXPLODE path consumes the shared sweep.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — reuse `spawnExplosionParticles` /
  `getExplosionVfxCounts`; add a completion-aware spawn option only if needed.
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` — expose/retain live minions long enough for the
  sweep to explode them (e.g. a read-before-destroy accessor).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — existing `destroySelf()` / `playExplosion(scale)`
  seams consumed by the sweep (no reward side effects).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — gym destroy seam used by the
  sweep in the gym.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§3.3, §4.4.4),
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — defeat-flow documentation.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — parity guards that must keep passing.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z (completed) — mini-boss epic; this sweep refines its
  defeat behaviour.
- AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5 (completed) — `PlayScene` mini-boss integration
  (`_damageMiniBoss` defeat path this change extends).
- AH-0MVCRAV3B0069AIJ (completed) — `WaveManager` per-level mini-boss gating
  (the wave-advance-once constraint).
- AH-0MVH85XXZ008INE2 (completed) — mini-boss left-behind graphics; precedent
  for tearing the encounter down cleanly on defeat.
- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH (completed) — mini-boss reward overlay
  (`openMiniBossReward`, `miniBossRewardOpen`), the overlay this change delays.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F (completed) — reward-overlay demo auto-select; must not
  stall behind the new delay.
- AH-0MVCB6LBE007I6R8 (open) — "Stop firing when boss is destroyed": related
  post-destruction cleanup pattern at the final boss; check for a shared
  "defeat moment" seam rather than duplicating gating logic.
- AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB (completed) — staggered
  multi-burst celebration scheduling (`spawnVictoryFireworks`) to mirror.
- AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY (open) — "Explosions sould be explosions": image-based
  explosion rendering; overlaps the VFX module but is orthogonal (visual
  quality vs defeat-sweep behaviour).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (completed) — the shared particle explosion module this
  change reuses.

Duplicate check: performed (keywords "explosions", "mini-boss", "reward
screen", "chain explosion") — **no overlapping completed item found**; the
nearest items (VFX quality AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY, final-boss victory fireworks
AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) do not cover a mini-boss-defeat
explosion sweep.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** applies to the **mini-boss defeat only**. Extending the
  sweep to the final boss or ordinary wave clears is separate work (record as
  discovered work items, not scope).
- **Particle budget:** up to 40 bursts in a short window. Mitigation: extra and
  anchored bursts use a modest enemy-scale size/scale and a reduced particle
  count; the sweep is bounded by `max(0, 30 − n) + 10 + n ≤ 40` bursts.
- **Double-advance risk:** `_damageMiniBoss` already has a stale-count
  reconciliation that can replay `onEnemyDestroyed`; sweeping enemies changes
  the alive count, so tests must assert the level advance fires exactly once,
  after the sweep.
- **Minion teardown ordering** (see Constraints) — capture before destroy, or
  minions vanish without exploding and `n` is under-counted.
- **Pause ordering:** the overlay's pause freezes tweens; completion must be
  driven by real tween completion (or an explicit timer derived from burst
  lifespan + stagger), not by a frame count that could be frozen.
- **Assumption:** the 10 mini-boss bursts are anchored at the death position
  captured at destruction (same discipline as the victory fireworks anchor), not
  at the entity's (already destroyed) live coordinates.
- **Assumption:** "scattered randomly across the scene" means uniformly sampled
  within the playfield inset by the burst radius, so no explosion is clipped
  entirely off-screen. If the producer expects the full screen edge-to-edge,
  only the inset constant changes.
- **Assumption:** the sweep is a visual-only celebration; the mini-boss reward
  remains the only reward for the encounter (operator Q2 = B + C).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Per entry: question, answer, answering party, evidence.

- **Q1 (scope of "all remaining enemies")** — "Which live entities count as
  'all remaining enemies' and explode on the sweep: (a) everything alive on the
  field — escort ships, mini-boss-summoned minions, and hazards (asteroids, lane
  traffic); (b) wave-gating enemies only (escorts + minions, exclude hazards);
  or (c) escort ships only (exclude minions and hazards)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "1. B"** — wave-gating enemies only: escort ships plus
  the mini-boss's live minions; hazards (asteroids, lane traffic) are excluded
  and survive. Recommended option was (b); operator selected (b). Source:
  interactive reply. Research: `PlayScene.spawned` holds one entry per live
  entity including hazards; `isNonBlockingHazard`
  (`src/scenes/core/waveTimeout.ts`) is the shared hazard classifier, and
  `MiniBoss.getMinions()` exposes the entity-owned minions.
- **Q2 (kill semantics)** — "Should sweep-destroyed enemies be real kills — (a)
  full shared kill path (score, mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops, telemetry)
  with wave-advance batched to sweep end; (b) cosmetic explosions only —
  enemies removed visually, no score/drops; or (c) destroyed without any reward
  or telemetry?"
  — **Answer (operator): "2. B + C"** — treat as (b) cosmetic explosions only
  **and** (c) no reward or telemetry: enemies are removed visually with their
  explosion VFX, and award no score, no mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops and no
  kill telemetry (wave bookkeeping still updates so the level completes). Source:
  interactive reply. Recommended option was (a); operator overrode it with
  B + C. Research: `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` is the reward-bearing path and
  must **not** be used by the sweep; `BaseEnemy.destroySelf()` marks the entity
  dead and plays its explosion only, so it is the correct seam.
- **Q3 (count formula edges)** — "With n remaining enemies, the spec says
  `30 − n` extra scattered explosions. When n ≥ 30 (or 0), what should happen:
  (a) clamp extra at 0 — total scattered bursts = `max(30, n)` from enemy bursts
  + extras, plus the fixed 10 at the mini-boss; (b) always fire at least 30
  scattered extras regardless of n; or (c) always fire exactly 30 scattered
  extras on top of the n enemy bursts (total `30 + n`)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "3. A"** — clamp the extra count at 0:
  `extras = max(0, 30 − n)`, so `n = 0` gives 30 extras and `n ≥ 30` gives none;
  the 10 mini-boss-anchored bursts are always additional. Source: interactive
  reply. Recommended option was (a); operator selected (a). Research: at a clean
  defeat `n` is usually small (escorts cleared first), but carry-over survivors
  and minions can push `n` higher, so the clamp keeps the display bounded
  (`total bursts ≤ n + max(0, 30 − n) + 10 ≤ 40`).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVBMESIE003YQ68** – AI should focus fire on the boss (open)
- **AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5** – PlayScene mini-boss integration (completed)
- **AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F** – AI bot does not know how to select upgrade in mini-boss reward screen (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muwz5hcv0034h44, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvcrbno6003e1ch, 0mvj8u79v0056i2f, ac1 (+453 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvj8u79v0056i2f, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+425 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvcrav3b0069aij, 0mvcrbisu006nun5, ac1, ac2 (+407 more)

## Appendix: Producer review follow-up (2026-10-29)

The first implementation was **rejected by manual review** with: "Enemies
explode but the mini-boss itself needs to be more explosive. Cluster another
20 explosions in and around the mini-boss, with 2 going off every 0.25 of a
second."

Interpretation adopted (recorded in AC9):

- **"another 20"** — the 10 anchored bursts from AC2 are retained and 20
  additional finale bursts are added, giving 30 mini-boss-centred bursts.
- **"in and around"** — finale bursts are sampled uniformly inside a wider

  cluster (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_ANCHOR_SPREAD_PX` = 80 px), so some land inside

# Test: tracked-CSV suite-write regression guard

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12 (plan phase; test-first item — created first)

## Summary

Add the automated regression guard that proves a full-suite run never modifies the
tracked config CSVs (`src/data/ship-config.csv`, `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`,
`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`) in **either** the active worktree **or** the main
checkout. This is the acceptance test for the parent bug: it must fail loudly when a
later change reintroduces a leaked CSV write.

## User story

As a developer/agent running the suite, I want the suite itself to assert that no tracked
CSV changed during the run, so a leaked write fails the run immediately instead of tripping
the implement dirty-tree gate hours later.

## Scope

- A Vitest `globalSetup`/teardown pair (new small module, e.g.
  `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.globalSetup.ts` plus a testable helper) registered in
  `vitest.config.ts` for both `unit` and `integration` projects.
- Snapshot the content hash (sha256) of the three tracked CSVs in the active checkout at
  suite start; resolve the main checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (worktrees
  share the main `.git`, so `dirname` of the common dir is the main checkout) and snapshot
  its CSVs too when the path differs and the files exist.
- On teardown, compare; if any file changed, throw with the offending path(s), the
  checkout, and the pre/post git diff hint so the failure is actionable.
- A pure unit test for the comparison/reporting helper (changed / unchanged / missing /
  non-git checkout cases) so the guard logic itself is covered without needing a leak.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 1 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **No tracked-file writes from suites** — Running the audit-accepted full suite (`npm --silent test`: `unit` + `integration` projects) from a worktree leaves every tracked `src/data/*.csv` (`ship-config.csv`, `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`) unchanged in **both** the active worktree and the main checkout. Verified by an automated pre/post `git status --porcelain` of both checkouts that runs as part of the change's tests (a regression guard the suite itself asserts).

- `npm --silent test` registers the guard for both projects; a full suite run leaves all
  three tracked CSVs byte-identical in the active checkout and the main checkout.
- The guard is proven effective: a deliberate in-test write to a tracked CSV (or a
  temporary mutation performed inside the guard's own unit test) makes the guard report the
  changed file and fail — the check is not vacuous.
- Guard degrades safely: outside a git repository, or when the main checkout path is
  unresolvable, it logs a skip reason and does not fail the run.
- Guard teardown never writes to the watched files and never itself dirties the tree
  (`git status --porcelain` is unchanged by a suite run apart from intended test output).
- The helper's unit tests pass and are included in the existing `unit` project selection.

## Key Files

- `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.ts` — hash/compare/report helper (pure, unit-testable).
- `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.test.ts` — unit tests for the helper.
- `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.globalSetup.ts` — Vitest global setup returning the teardown.
- `vitest.config.ts` — register `globalSetup` for the `unit` and `integration` projects.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — reference for the tracked CSV list; do not duplicate logic.

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Helper: `snapshotTrackedCsvs(repoRoots: string[]) -> Map<path, hash>`,
   `diffSnapshots(before, after) -> string[]` and a formatter for the failure message.
2. Global setup: resolve the active root from `process.cwd()` and the main checkout from
   `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; return a teardown closure that diffs and throws.
3. Unit-test the helper's diff/format paths, including a real temp-dir mutation.
4. Register in `vitest.config.ts` for both projects; run the changed-scope suite via
   `/skill:test` to confirm green.

## Notes / risks

- Do **not** shell out to `git status` for the assertion (porcelain output is noisier than
  content hashes and cannot distinguish checkouts); use content hashes and keep git only
  for locating the main checkout.
- The guard is expected to be committed **before** the fixes (TDD); it should pass on a
  clean run and only fail if a leak recurs.
- Overlap: `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` already validates CSV *content* in the active
  checkout; this item adds the cross-checkout write guard, it does not replace the seed
  tests.

# Feature: CSV plugin root isolation and escape refusal

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12

## Summary

Replace the CSV dev-server plugin's implicit `process.cwd()` write root with an explicit,
verified root derived from the Vite-resolved project root, and refuse any request whose
resolved target escapes that root (no file I/O, HTTP error plus a logged reason).

## User story

As a test-suite/CI operator, I want the CSV plugin to be incapable of writing outside the
checkout it is serving, so a suite run can never clobber the main checkout's tracked CSVs
through a symlinked `node_modules` / mis-inferred project root.

## Scope

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`:
  - Resolve the root inside `configureServer` as
    `options.root ?? server.config.root` (Vite resolves `server.config.root` from the
    config file's directory, so it stays in the active checkout instead of following
    `process.cwd()`); keep `options.root` as an explicit override for the existing
    temp-fixture tests.
  - Add a containment guard: for both GET and PUT, `resolve(root, relPath)` must stay inside
    the resolved root (`path.relative` check plus a `..`/absolute-path check, not naive
    `startsWith`); otherwise respond `403` with
    `{ ok: false, error: 'target escapes project root' }` and log the reason, performing no
    filesystem access.
  - Update the `ConfigCsvPluginOptions.root` doc comment and the factory doc comment to
    describe the new root semantics.
- `vite.config.ts`: only touch if the plugin cannot self-derive the root; keep
  `configCsvPlugin()` optionless when `server.config.root` suffices.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 2 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Root isolation in the plugin** — The CSV plugin never resolves write targets to a checkout other than the active project root: the implicit `process.cwd()` default is replaced by an explicit, verified root (derived from the Vite-resolved root, or an explicit option), and any request whose resolved target escapes the active root is refused with no file I/O (HTTP error + logged reason). Existing explicit-root test fixtures keep working unchanged.

- With no `root` option, a plugin configured against a fake `ViteDevServer` whose
  `config.root` is a temp dir writes only inside that temp dir — never to
  `process.cwd()` (asserted by a test that sets `process.cwd()` elsewhere and checks the
  cwd CSV is untouched).
- A request whose `relPath` escapes the root (`../` traversal, URL-encoded traversal,
  absolute path) is refused with HTTP 403, no file created/modified on disk, and a
  logged reason; covered for both GET and PUT.
- Existing explicit-root fixtures in `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` and
  `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` keep passing unchanged.
- Valid in-root writes keep atomic-write (temp file + rename) behaviour and the existing
  upsert/append semantics; `isDevServer`/`apply: 'serve'` gating is unchanged.
- The plugin's own tests pass in the `unit` project selection.

## Key Files

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — root resolution, containment guard, doc comments.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — new default-root and escape-refusal tests.
- `vite.config.ts` — only if an explicit root must be passed; otherwise untouched.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — regression check only (explicit root path).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — reference for the codec/validation helpers; not expected to change.

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Move `root` resolution into `configureServer`; keep `options.root` precedence.
2. Add `isWithinRoot(root, filePath)` helper plus a `403` refusal branch used by both
   handlers before any `existsSync`/`readFileSync`/`atomicWrite`.
3. Add the two tests (default-root isolation, escape refusal for GET and PUT).
4. Update the option/factory doc comments; run the changed-scope suite via `/skill:test`.

## Notes / risks

- Do not weaken the guard for the legit dev workflow: `npm run dev` in the active checkout
  must still persist saves to the committed CSVs (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA).
- Symlink caveat: compare real paths (`realpath`) where available so a symlinked
  `node_modules` cannot make a legitimate active root look foreign — but a *target* outside
  the root must always be refused.
- Guard reads as well as writes (the parent AC says "any request"); this is deliberate and
  should be noted in the code comment.

# Feature: Test-mode write guard in configStore

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12

## Summary

Add a test-harness guard in `src/core/configStore.ts` so `saveShipConfig`,
`saveEnemyConfig` and `saveDifficultyCurves` can never write a tracked repository file
under vitest: in test mode they update the in-memory registry only and perform no network
I/O.

## User story

As a test author, I want store saves under vitest to be hermetic (registry-only, no disk,
no network), so a test can exercise save behaviour without any chance of PUTing through a
live dev server into a checkout.

## Scope

- `src/core/configStore.ts`:
  - Add `isTestMode()` = `import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'`, next to `isDev()`/`isSsr()`,
    with a doc comment explaining why it exists (belt-and-braces against the relative
    `/api/csv/...` fetch resolving against the happy-dom origin).
  - In each save function, after the `isDev()` gate, short-circuit in test mode: apply the
    same registry mutation the success path applies (including the difficulty-curve
    `generation` normalisation), skip `putCsv`, skip `reReadRegistry`, return `{ ok: true }`.
  - Document the resulting save semantics (registry-only in test mode) on the three
    exported save functions.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts`: direct unit tests for the guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 3 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Test-mode write guard in the store** — Under the vitest/test harness (`import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'` detected in `configStore.ts`), `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` must never write a tracked repository file: they either update the registry only (documented no-op wrt disk, preserving registry semantics used by tests) or route writes to an isolated temp fixture. A direct unit test covers each save function under test mode asserting no file on disk changes.

- Under `MODE === 'test'` (`vi.stubEnv('MODE', 'test')` with `DEV` true), each of
  `saveShipConfig`, `saveEnemyConfig` and `saveDifficultyCurves` resolves `{ ok: true }`
  while performing **no** `fetch` (asserted with a spy/stub that fails the test if called)
  and leaving every tracked CSV byte-identical (hash check).
- Registry semantics are preserved: after a test-mode ship save, `loadShipConfig()` (and the
  equivalent enemy/difficulty accessors) return the saved values; the difficulty-curve
  `generation` normalisation still applies.
- In non-test dev mode (`MODE` not `test`, `DEV` true) the existing write path is
  unchanged: the save still PUTs through `putCsv` and re-reads the registry (asserted with
  the existing fetch-bridge pattern in a temp root).
- Outside dev mode the existing `WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` behaviour is unchanged.
- All new and existing `src/core/configStore*.test.ts` tests pass in their projects.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `isTestMode()`, save-function short-circuit, doc comments.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` — test-mode guard unit tests.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — reference for the explicit-root fetch bridge
  pattern; adjust only if the guard changes its expectations.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — reference for default ship/enemy values.

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Add `isTestMode()` beside `isDev()`/`isSsr()` with the rationale comment.
2. Add the guard branch to `saveShipConfig` (registry update + `{ ok: true }`), then mirror
   it for `saveEnemyConfig` and `saveDifficultyCurves`.
3. Unit-test each save function in test mode: no fetch, no disk change, registry updated.
4. One dev-mode control test proving the real write path still runs; run the changed-scope
   suite via `/skill:test`.

## Notes / risks

- Do not gate on `isDev() === false` (that would flip existing dev-mode assertions); the
  guard is an additional, earlier exit for `MODE === 'test'` only.
- A test-mode caller that expects a *failure* result (`ok: false`) must now stub the store
  function or assert the registry-only contract — check `GymPlayer.test.ts`,
  `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` and gym save tests for such assumptions.
- Documented divergence: in test mode the registry is authoritative and disk is not, which
  matches how the mocked-store gym tests already behave.

# Task: Hermetic fetch handling for relative CSV calls in happy-dom

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12

## Summary

Close the escape route at the harness level: in the `integration` (happy-dom) project, a
relative `/api/csv/...` fetch must never reach a stray real server (whose root may be the
main checkout). Install a default fetch guard in `src/test/setup.ts` that refuses such
requests unless a test explicitly installs its own bridge, and document the pattern.

## User story

As a test author, I want an accidental un-bridged `/api/csv/...` call to fail loudly and
locally instead of silently PUTing into whichever server happens to answer
`http://localhost:3000`.

## Scope

- `src/test/setup.ts` (integration project only): install a default `fetch` wrapper that
  - passes non-`/api/csv/` requests through to the native fetch,
  - for `/api/csv/...` requests without an installed bridge, rejects (or returns a
    synthetic `503` with a clear message) naming the test file and pointing at the bridge
    helper, without performing any network I/O.
  - keeps `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …)` bridges (used by `configStore.integration.test.ts`)
    working: the wrapper only applies when no per-test stub replaced the global.
- Add/centralise a small bridge helper (e.g. `src/test/csvFetchBridge.ts`) so a test opts in
  with one call, mirroring the existing `installFetchBridge` in
  `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts`.
- Add the documenting comment in the integration tests that exercise real saves: relative
  fetches resolve against the happy-dom origin, so every real save **must** install the
  bridge; note the `configStore` test-mode guard as the second line of defence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 4 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Escape route closed** — No test can PUT through a live dev-server endpoint by accident: relative `/api/csv/...` fetches in the happy-dom project must resolve against a test-controlled origin (explicit bridge/stub), never a stray `localhost` server that could answer from the main checkout. Add a comment in the integration tests documenting the relative-fetch/bridge pattern and verifying the bridge is installed for every real save.

- In the `integration` project, an un-bridged relative `/api/csv/...` fetch fails the test
  with a message naming the file and the bridge helper; no real network request is made
  (asserted with a native-fetch spy that must not be called).
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` keeps passing with its explicit bridge and
  temp root; the bridge helper is reused rather than duplicated if that is a pure
  refactor.
- The guard is a no-op for non-CSV requests (e.g. telemetry upload, asset fetches) so no
  existing integration test regresses.
- A comment in the integration tests documents the relative-fetch/happy-dom origin hazard
  and the requirement to install the bridge for every real save.
- Full `integration` project suite passes via `/skill:test`.

## Key Files

- `src/test/setup.ts` — default fetch guard for `/api/csv/...`.
- `src/test/csvFetchBridge.ts` — shared bridge helper (new, small).
- `src/test/csvFetchBridge.test.ts` — unit tests for the guard/helper.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — reuse the helper, add the documenting comment.
- `vitest.config.ts` — reference only (`setupFiles: ['src/test/setup.ts']`).

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Write the guard helper + unit tests (un-bridged rejection, bridged pass-through,
   non-CSV pass-through).
2. Wire it into `src/test/setup.ts` for the integration project.
3. Reuse it in `configStore.integration.test.ts` and add the documenting comment.
4. Run the changed-scope suite via `/skill:test` to confirm no integration regressions.

## Notes / risks

- `vi.stubGlobal`/`vi.unstubAllGlobals` ordering matters: if the default guard is installed
  at module scope it must be re-installed after `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in `afterEach`;
  document the resolution in the helper.
- Do not simply hard-stub `fetch` globally — that would break legit non-CSV fetches in
  scene/telemetry tests.
- Overlap: this item is complementary to the `configStore` test-mode guard (which prevents
  the fetch from being issued at all); both are required by the parent ACs.

# Fail fast on unwritable --out and invalid tune CSV

## Goal (user story)
As a developer running tune-loop verification I want `--tune` to validate `--out` (and the
balance CSV path) before anything expensive starts, so an invalid path fails in seconds with
an actionable message instead of running both sweeps first and then hanging or dying.

## Problem
`scripts/evaluate.mjs` only touches the output directory after both batches have run:
`executeTune()` calls `mkdirSync(options.outputDir, {recursive: true})` *after* the candidate
sweep (line ~394) and `main()` does the same for the non-tune path (line ~441). The 2026-10-21
negative probe (`--out /proc/nope/x`, 2 games x 200 ticks) therefore ran both sweeps and then
stalled for 166.6 minutes before an external SIGKILL (parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune --set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=7 --games 2 --ticks 200 --out <unwritable>`
  exits non-zero in well under two seconds, printing a single clear diagnostic on stderr.
- The probe runs **before** `loadCore()` (no Vite SSR boot) and before any `--tune` sweep.
- The `--tune` CSV target (`src/data/<tuneFile>`) is validated up-front too: a missing or
  unreadable CSV fails fast with its own message instead of failing after a baseline sweep.

1. Add an exported, unit-testable probe to `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, e.g.
   `ensureWritableOutputDir(dir)` → `{ok: true}` | `{ok: false, code, message}`:

# Journal the tune CSV edit so a hard kill cannot leave it dirty

## Goal (user story)
As a developer I want the tune/edit cycle crash-safe, so that even an external SIGKILL, OOM or
timeout kill of the CLI never leaves `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` edited in the worktree — or,
if it does, the very next invocation (or a documented one-line command) restores it exactly.

## Problem
`executeTune()` applies the edit through `applyCsvEditFile()` and restores it in a `finally`
via `restoreCsvFile()` using the in-memory `attempt.originalText`. A SIGKILL runs no `finally`,
so the edited CSV survives the process (observed on 2026-10-21 immediately after the exit-137
kill, parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- Before the first edited byte is written, a small journal (target path + original bytes) is
  persisted beside the CSV and fsynced.
- The journal is git-ignored, so a crashed run never shows up as a worktree change.
- After a successful restore (or with `--keep-edit`) the journal is removed.
- Any subsequent `scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` invocation that finds a stale journal first
  reconciles it (restores the original bytes, removes the journal, prints a warning) and then
  proceeds — so no manual step is needed in the normal case.
- A documented manual repair path exists for the case where the CSV must be restored without
  running the CLI again.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. New module `scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs`:
   `writeJournal(csvPath, originalBytes)` — write `<csvPath>.tune-journal` (JSON: csvPath,
   base64 original, pid, ISO timestamp) to a temp name, `fsync`, `rename` (atomic);
   `readJournal(path)`; `clearJournal(path)`; `reconcileJournal(path)` — restore original
   bytes when the journal exists, then delete it, returning `{action: 'restored'|'none'}`.
2. Wire into `executeTune()`: write the journal before `applyCsvEditFile`'s write, and clear
   it inside the existing `finally` after `restoreCsvFile()` resolves.
3. `main()` reconciles a stale journal for the `--tune` target before validation proceeds.
4. Add the journal pattern to `.gitignore` (e.g. `src/data/*.tune-journal`).
5. Document the guarantee + repair commands in `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop →

# Per-run progress output and opt-in sweep watchdog

## Goal (user story)
As a developer (or an agent) running a long tune sweep I want visible per-run progress and an
opt-in bounded-runtime guard, so an abnormal run can never stall silently for hours and so a
timeout aborts cleanly with the CSV already restored.

## Problem
`--tune` prints nothing between start and the final summary: `executeTune()` runs two
`runBalanceBatch()` sweeps with no output. When the 2026-10-21 negative probe stalled, the only
signal was a silent process for 166.6 minutes until an external SIGKILL (parent item
AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B). After slice 2 the known hang is gone, but a future stall in the sweep
itself (configuration-driven blow-up, non-determinism guard loop, I/O stall) would again be
invisible.

## Expected behaviour
- Every `--tune` run writes one progress line per completed game to **stderr**:
  `[tune] baseline 1/2 seed=1 policy=competent`, then `[tune] candidate 2/2 …`, then the phase
  transitions (edit applied, comparing, restoring). Stdout stays byte-identical to today so
  artifact/print parity and determinism are preserved.
- `--watchdog <seconds>` (default `0` = off) arms a bounded-runtime guard: on expiry the run
  prints a diagnostic naming the phase and the elapsed time, restores the CSV (journal from
  slice 3 + synchronous restore), and exits with a distinct code (124) rather than leaving a
  killed-but-dirty worktree.
- `--help` and `docs/BALANCING.md` document both.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Reuse the existing per-run hook instead of adding a second mechanism: `runBatch` already
   accepts `config.onRun` (`src/ai/eval/engine.ts`), but `runBalanceBatch()` in
   `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` does not expose it (and `CliOptions.telemetrySink` is ignored there).
   Add an optional second parameter `runBalanceBatch(options, hooks?: {onRun?})` that forwards
   `onRun`; keep the existing signature/behaviour when `hooks` is omitted.
2. In `executeTune()`, pass an `onRun` that writes the progress line to `io.err` (count games
   against `sweep.seeds.length * policies.length`) — no divergent copy of the sweep logic.
3. Add `--watchdog <seconds>` parsing to `parseEvaluateArgs` (validated: finite, >= 0;
   non-numeric → usage error exit 2), arm a timer in `executeTune()` and clear it in the
   existing `finally`; on expiry: diagnostic + `restoreCsvFile` + `process.exitCode = 124`
   (use `exitCode`, not `exit()`, so pending stderr drains and the pipe cannot mask the exit).
4. Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md` tune flags table + "Guards and guarantees"; assert in
   `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Risky assumptions
- A watchdog timer inside a synchronous sweep cannot interrupt a *blocking* synchronous call —
  it only fires between runs. Recorded as an accepted limitation: the guard catches stalls that
  yield to the event loop (the observed case is caught by slice 2's fail-fast path instead), and
  the progress lines remain the primary signal for a truly blocking stall. Document this
  limitation in `docs/BALANCING.md`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- src/ai/eval/cli.ts
- src/ai/eval/engine.ts
- src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every --tune run emits per-run progress lines on stderr (never stdout), covered by a unit test that captures both streams.
2. An opt-in bounded-runtime watchdog (--watchdog <seconds>) aborts the sweep with a clear diagnostic naming the stalled phase, restores the CSV, and exits with a distinct non-zero code, covered by a test.
3. The full verification command used in AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (including the negative probe) completes without hanging, with elapsed times recorded in a work-item comment.
4. Progress wiring reuses the shared runBatch onRun hook through runBalanceBatch (no divergent sweep copy in the shell), covered by cli.test.ts.
5. Artifact/print parity is preserved: stdout and the four tune artifacts are byte-identical to the pre-change output for the same seed/options (determinism tests stay green).
6. --help and docs/BALANCING.md document --watchdog, its default (off), its exit code, and the accepted limitation that a blocking synchronous stall cannot be interrupted, asserted by the docs guard.

**As a designer**, I want the campaign-wide variety rules expressed as one shared, pure analysis module with automated tests, so future wave edits cannot silently reintroduce sequential repetition (parent AC1–AC3).

1. A new pure module `src/waves/campaignVariety.ts` (no Phaser/runtime import) exporting:

   - `LEVEL_IDENTITY` — the documented dominant archetype per level (L1 scout, L2 diver, L3 tank, L4 mixed/firestorm, L5 phaser, L6 march, L7 tank+ghost segmented, L8 lane/raider, L9 phaser, L10 gauntlet mix), each entry carrying the GDD §3.2 reference in a comment.

## Goal

As a player I want an unmistakable hyperspace "warp" when the background changes between levels, and as a developer I want that effect to be a deterministic, time-boxed, individually switchable module with a testable timeline, so level changes read as a jump through space without ever hurting readability or blocking play.

## Background

Producer answer Q2 (2026-10-25): **Option A — hyperspace-style one-shot** (converging streak overlay + radial scale distortion + brief flash/crossfade), timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s, currently exported from `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`). Existing VFX modules show the house pattern to copy: exported tuning constants plus per-layer `*_ENABLE_*` toggles and caller-owned effect registries that are destroyed on `SHUTDOWN` (`src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`, `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`).

Import direction matters: `PlayScene` imports VFX modules, so a VFX module must **not** import `PlayScene`. The duration therefore moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and is re-exported from `PlayScene` for existing importers.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and `PlayScene` re-exports it unchanged, so `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` can derive `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` from the same single source (no duplicated literal); all existing importers (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`) keep compiling without edits.
2. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` exposes the full timeline as exported constants (streak phase, distortion/scale phase, flash/crossfade phase) whose phases are ordered, non-overlapping and sum to the total duration; a test asserts the sum and ordering so the effect can never outlive the transition window.
3. The effect renders three layers — converging streak overlay, radial scale distortion, brief flash/crossfade into the incoming background — each with its own `BACKGROUND_WARP_ENABLE_*` toggle (following the `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_*` pattern) and exported magnitudes (streak count, speed, colours, scale range, flash alpha).
4. Deterministic: no `Math.random()` (or a seeded generator) — two runs from the same inputs produce byte-identical layer parameters, asserted by test. Time-boxed and observable: an `update(dt)`-style tick API (no reliance on wall-clock tweens) so a test can advance exactly `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` and assert completion; `isComplete()` is true at the end and never before.
5. Bounded and disposable: a fixed maximum streak count (constant), all display objects inside one container, `destroy()` idempotent, and a test asserts the container/children are gone after completion and after an early `destroy()` (no leaks if the scene restarts mid-warp).
6. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` covers the ACs above; changed-scope tests and `tsc --noEmit` pass.

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC2 "changes exactly on level change", AC3 warp timing/does-not-block, AC6 integration tests).

## Goal

As a player I want the new level's background to arrive with the warp exactly when the level changes (and never mid-level), so each of the ten levels is unmistakably a different place in space while gameplay, input and wave timing are untouched.

## Background

Level changes flow `WaveManager.onEnemyDestroyed()` → `'levelCleared'` → `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` → `_announceLevel()` + `_startTransition()` (`LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS = 1.5`). Two facts shape this slice:

1. **Two handlers.** The `levelCleared` case is duplicated in `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` and in `PlayScene._advanceAfterTimeout()` (the wave-timer expiry path). Both must reach the background swap, so the `levelCleared` work is extracted into one helper (e.g. `_onLevelCleared()`) that both call — otherwise a level cleared by timeout skips the swap.
2. **Level is already advanced.** `WaveManager` increments `_levelIndex` *before* returning `'levelCleared'`, so `waveManager.level` during the transition is the **incoming** level: the swap target is `backgroundForLevel(waveManager.level)`, and the warp must finish no later than `transitionTimer` reaches 0 (`_onTransitionComplete()` then spawns the new wave).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On `'levelCleared'` only — not on `'waveCleared'`, not on `'bossTriggered'`, not per wave — `PlayScene` starts the warp and swaps to `backgroundForLevel(waveManager.level)`; the same code path is reached by both the kill path (`_handleWaveEvent`) and the wave-timeout path (`_advanceAfterTimeout`), with no duplicated background logic between them.
2. The warp is created at `_startTransition()` time for a level change, advanced from the scene's own tick (not wall-clock tweens), and is complete by the time the transition ends: after ticking `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` the background's `textureKey()` equals `backgroundForLevel(newLevel)`, `isComplete()` is true, and `_onTransitionComplete()` has spawned the wave on the unchanged frame schedule.
3. Non-blocking: during the warp the player still moves, auto-fires and can teleport, and the transition/wave timer schedule is unchanged — asserted by a test that ticks half the transition while driving input and checks bullets/position, plus an assertion that `transitionRemaining()` is unaffected by the warp's presence.
4. Boss entry keeps the final level's background (documented decision: no swap and no warp on `'bossTriggered'`); asserted by test so the boss arena's backdrop is deterministic.
5. Restart/shutdown safety: starting a new run or shutting the scene down mid-warp leaves no warp container, no stale background and no leaked timer — a subsequent level change behaves normally (tested).
6. New integration suite `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` covers ACs 1–5 and the existing `PlayScene` suites (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `PlaySceneHUD.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still pass unchanged; full-suite gate is left to the dev-push gate (no ad-hoc full runs).

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #6 — "Tests cover: deterministic level→background mapping, swap fires on level change (not wave), warp effect activates during the transition and completes within its duration, and the background layer does not intercept input; document updates (README, code comments, credits/attribution file with licences, GDD §3.2/§7.1 references as needed); the full project test suite passes with the new changes." — specifically the integration-tests half (swap-on-level-change-only, timing, input non-blocking, full suite); the documentation half is AH-0MVSEC4RS003KQGV; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` first (boot via `src/test/gameHarness.ts`, drain a level to force `'levelCleared'`, use the fixture textures from the shared-layer slice).
- Extract `_onLevelCleared()` on `PlayScene`; both `_handleWaveEvent` and `_advanceAfterTimeout` call it (per the parent's "shared behaviour lives once" rule).
- In `_startTransition()`, take an optional `levelChanged` flag (or compare target level against the currently shown one) to start the warp; keep `_startTransition` otherwise identical so wave transitions are unaffected.

## Summary

Author the deterministic unit tests that pin the 100-slot wheel distribution
and the weighted outcome resolver **before** the module exists, so the
implementation is driven by tests rather than retrofitted. The tests live in
`src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts` and import only the new pure
module `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` — no Phaser, no scene, no `Player`.

## What the tests must pin

- **Distribution** — the 100 slots are exactly 1 bonus + 5 three-upgrade +
  10 two-upgrade + 84 one-upgrade, exposed as a single shared constant and
  verified by an exhaustive slot-index sweep (no statistical tolerance).
- **Distinct multi-picks** — a 3-upgrade slot with ≥ 3 owned kinds upgrades
  three *distinct* kinds; a 2-upgrade slot with ≥ 2 owned kinds upgrades two
  distinct kinds; a repeat happens only when there are fewer owned kinds than
  picks (one owned kind landing a 3-slot gains +3 levels on it).
- **Bonus** — the bonus outcome grants +1 level to **every** owned permanent
  kind.
- **Pool coverage** — owned kinds come from the shared six-slot accounting, so
  the tests cover both halves of the shared pool (power-up kinds and weapon
  drops) and never include the permanent cannon or the `reset` utility.
- **Determinism** — the same run seed plus the same owned-kind snapshot
  reproduces the same outcome; a source-scan assertion proves the module
  contains no `Math.random()` and no wall-clock read.
- **Purity** — the module imports neither Phaser nor any scene module.

## Landing (test-first pair)

This item and its paired implementation item share one branch: the tests are
committed **first** (failing for the right reason, recorded in an item
comment) and the pair is closed together once the implementation makes them
green. Red tests are never pushed to `dev` on their own.

## Summary

Rework `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward` / `selectMiniBossReward` so a mini-boss
defeat launches the wheel overlay with the owned permanent kinds, applies the
resolved outcome exactly once through the shared reward machinery, falls back
to the hold-full-style three-option choice when nothing permanent is owned,
and keeps the demo auto-spin. The unlock machinery is already removed (parent
AC5, sibling item).

## Design

- Open: build the owned-kind snapshot once from
  `resolvePlayerSlotState(this.player).ownedIds`
  (power-up kinds and weapon drops; permanent view). When empty →
  **fallback**: open the shared `MineralChoiceScene` with the hold-full-style
  three options (`createRandomChoiceStrategy` / `chooseOptions`), applied
  permanently — a mini-boss always pays out (AC4).
- When populated: resolve the wheel outcome once from the run-seeded RNG
  (`drawWheelOutcome`/`miniBossWheel`) and launch `MiniBossWheelScene` with the
  wedges, the outcome and a single result callback. Pause exactly like the
  hold-full choice; pass the frozen fire schedule for the reduced-volume ghost
  fire; rebase the beat clock on resume.
- Select/result: apply the outcome once via `applyWheelOutcome`
  (shared reward seam), close the overlay, resume play, reset the open flag —
  a repeated select is a no-op.
- Demo mode: pass `autoSpinMs: BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot
  auto-spins from the run-seeded RNG and never stalls.
- Test getters (`getMiniBossRewardOptions`, `isMiniBossRewardOpen`) preserved
  or re-homed so the wheel-flow tests keep a stable surface.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (rework `openMiniBossReward` /
  `selectMiniBossReward`; drop unlock state)
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (launched overlay)
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (outcome resolution + application)
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` (`resolvePlayerSlotState` — owned kinds)
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` (`chooseOptions` for the fallback)

  distribution and outcome resolver" and "Remove the weapon-unlock reward

# Temporary upgrades should always be temporary

**Type:** bug · **Priority:** high · **Stage:** intake_complete

## Original report

> When an upgrade/weapon is permanently owned and a temporary version of it is
> collected in level the increase in level should be temporary just as it would
> be if it was picked up without the permanent upgrade present.

## Problem statement

A field pickup is supposed to add a **temporary** level component that reverts
when its temporary window expires. For the seven power-ups that have no timed
effect, the temporary stack is never cleared, so a field pickup raises the
item's effective level **permanently for the rest of the run** — including when
it is collected on top of an already permanently-owned item. The same bug class
exists in the weapon path in the reverse order: a permanent (hold-full) grant
applied while a field-pickup window is active deletes the countdown but leaves
the temporary stack behind, so the level never reverts.

Empirically reproduced against `PowerUpLevelStore` + `EffectsRegistry` on
`5fb3f913` (permanent grant, then one field pickup, then 120 s):

| Power-up | Level after field pickup | Level after 120 s | Temp stacks |
|---|---|---|---|
| shield, speed_boost, magnet, mineral_scoop, force_field, frenzy, chrono, thorns, salvage | 2 | 1 (reverts) | 0 |
| **bomb, smart_bomb, strike, phase_shift, teleport, extra_life, mystery_ufo** | 2 | **2 (never reverts)** | **1** |

Because the untimed temporary stack is retained, every later use of the item
(another pickup's grant, a permanent bomb's pulse rate, a permanent drone's
stats, a levelled life/charge grant) is priced one level too high for the rest
of the run — the increase is not temporary.

## Users and user story

> As the player, when I collect a temporary version of an item I already own
> permanently, I expect the extra level to last only as long as that pickup's
> temporary window and then revert to my permanent level — the same way it
> behaves when I have no permanent copy of the item.

Stakeholders: the player (predictable, reversible power growth) and the
producer/balance owner (temporary pickups must never compound into permanent
power).

## Resolved decisions

1. **Expiry mechanism (Q1 → (a)) — every upgrade defines its TTL.** Every
   field pickup gets a real temporary window; the window length (TTL) is a
   property of the **upgrade item**, not one global constant.
   - **Timed effects** (shield, speed boost, magnet, mineral scoop, force
     field, frenzy, chrono, thorns, salvage, and timed weapons): the TTL is the
     item's existing **level-resolved effect duration** — already per-upgrade
     and already level-scaled (e.g. shield 15 s → 30 s). Behaviour unchanged.
   - **Instant effects** (bomb, smart bomb, orbital strike, phase shift,
     teleport, extra life, mystery UFO): each catalogue entry gains an explicit
     per-kind TTL. **Proposed values** (documented assumption, tune in the
     catalogue, no code change): bomb 10 s, smart bomb 10 s, orbital strike
     10 s, phase shift 15 s, teleport 15 s, extra life 10 s, mystery UFO 15 s.
     Rationale: 10 s mirrors the established weapon window, the defensive
     kinds (phase/teleport 15 s) mirror the shield-style window, and the UFO
     window (15 s) spans a full 5–8 s drone sortie. Values are deliberately
     short so a temporary level can never compound across a wave.
   - **Weapons** keep their existing 10 s window (`WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS`), exposed
     so a future weapon definition can declare its own TTL.
2. **Consumables do not time out (Q2).** Already-granted consumables (Extra
   Life lives, Phase Shift charges, Teleport uses) persist when the temporary
   level reverts; only the *level* reverts. The consumables themselves never
   carry a timer. Consistent with Resolved decision 1b on AH-0MUX802450085VZZ
   and with the producer's answer to Q2.
3. **Weapon stale-stack fix in scope (Q3).** A permanent grant applied while a
   field-pickup window is active must not strand the temporary stack; the
   weapon path is part of this item.

## Required behaviour

- Every field pickup adds a temporary level component with a per-upgrade TTL;
  at expiry the component is removed and the effective level reverts to the
  permanent level (or the item becomes inactive/unowned when no permanent
  level was earned).
- Permanent level increases come **only** from hold-full / mineral-choice
  rewards, and a permanent grant never leaves a stale temporary stack behind.
- Consumables already granted are **not clawed back** when the level reverts.
- The hold-full choice keeps pricing the **permanent** level only; the HUD
  shows the **effective** level with a countdown while the window is open and
  `∞` when it is not.
- The six-slot loadout releases a temporarily-held slot when the window
  expires, for every kind (today the seven instant kinds hold their slot
  forever).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 — **No temporary level is immortal.** After a field pickup of any
  power-up or weapon, the temporary level component is removed at its
  per-upgrade TTL, and the effective level reverts to the permanent level (or
  the item becomes inactive/unowned). Covers the seven instant kinds (`bomb`,
  `smart_bomb`, `strike`, `phase_shift`, `teleport`, `extra_life`,
  `mystery_ufo`) as well as the already-timed kinds.
- AC2 — **TTL is defined per upgrade, not globally.** Timed effects keep their
  level-resolved duration as the TTL; each instant kind declares its own TTL in
  the shared catalogue (no single hard-coded constant applies to every
  power-up), and changing an entry's TTL changes the revert time without code
  changes. Tests assert the per-kind TTLs and that a level-scaled timed effect
  keeps its level-scaled window.
- AC3 — **Permanent grant never leaves a stale temporary stack.** A hold-full
  reward applied while a field-pickup window is active either keeps the window
  and lets it expire (reverting the temporary component) or clears the
  temporary component immediately; in both cases the effective level ends at
  the permanent level. Applies to `Player.equipWeapon(id, true)` (which today
  deletes `_weaponTimers` but leaves `_tempWeaponStacks`) and to the power-up
  `collect(id, true)` path.
- AC4 — **Consumables persist.** Extra Life lives, Phase Shift charges and
  Teleport uses already granted by a temporary pickup survive the level revert
  (only the level reverts), and the consumables themselves never expire.
  Tests assert both the revert and the retained counts.
- AC5 — **Choice and HUD semantics unchanged.** The hold-full choice still
  offers/permanent-prices the permanent level only (no temporary inflation, no
  `★ New` regression), and the HUD shows the effective level with a live
  countdown while the window is open and `∞` afterwards.
- AC6 — **Slot accounting follows expiry.** A temporary stack releases its
  six-slot occupancy when its window expires for every kind, including the
  seven instant kinds.
- AC7 — **Gym↔game parity.** The revert behaviour is identical in `PlayScene`,
  every gym scene and the headless arena; the shared core carries the single
  implementation and the existing parity/equivalence guards pass. Any
  intentional divergence is recorded in this work item.
- AC8 — **Regression tests.** Tests cover, for every kind: permanent grant +
  field pickup → level rises → expiry reverts; field pickup only → expiry
  clears; permanent grant applied mid-window → no stale stack; per-kind TTL;
  consumables persist; run reset clears both components. At least one test is
  written first (failing red) and proves the current defect.
- AC9 — **Testing and validation.** Full project test suite must pass with the
  new changes.
- AC10 — **Documentation updated.** GDD §4.4.2/§4.4.3, module doc comments
  (`powerUpLevels.ts`, `effects.ts`, `Player.ts`, catalogue types) and any
  HUD/slot docs describe the per-upgrade TTL rule; the AH-0MUX802450085VZZ
  "Resolved decision 4" exception is superseded. All related documentation is
  updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any
  relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Keep the single source of truth: the permanent/temporary split stays in
  `PowerUpLevelStore` (power-ups) and `Player` (weapons). Do not add a second,
  parallel counter or per-scene timers.
- TTL is data, not a hard-coded cross-kind constant: per catalogue entry for
  instant kinds, per effect duration for timed kinds.
- Reuse the existing expiry path where possible (`clearTemporary`,
  `_expireTimedEffect`, `tickWeaponTimers`) rather than a new lifecycle.
- Do not change how the hold-full choice prices permanent levels, and do not
  claw back already-granted consumables.
- Keep gym↔game parity; no divergent copy in a gym.

## Existing state

- `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent=false)` adds a temporary stack;
  `clearTemporary(id)` removes it, but only the timed-effect expiry path calls
  it. `EffectsRegistry._applyTimedEffect` has no timed branch for `bomb`,
  `smart_bomb`, `strike`, `phase_shift`, `teleport`, `extra_life`,
  `mystery_ufo`, so nothing ever clears their temporary stack (documented as
  "Resolved decision 4: no temporary window" on AH-0MUX802450085VZZ).
- `Player.equipWeapon(id, true)` calls `_weaponTimers.delete(id)` (stopping the
  countdown) without clearing `_tempWeaponStacks`, so a field pickup collected
  before a hold-full grant becomes permanent.
- The timed kinds already behave correctly (verified empirically): permanent
  grant + field pickup shows level 2 with a countdown, then reverts to 1.
- `Player.equipWeapon(id, false)` on a permanent weapon is correct (level 2
  during the 10 s window, back to 1 afterwards).
- HUD rows for one-shot kinds (`bomb`, `smart_bomb`, `strike`) are only shown
  when permanent, so adding a window does not by itself add a HUD row.

## Desired change

Give every field pickup's temporary level a real, per-upgrade TTL so the
temporary component always reverts; add the TTL to instant-effect catalogue
entries and reuse the level-resolved effect duration for timed effects; clear
stale temporary components when a permanent grant lands; keep consumables and
permanent-pricing semantics intact. Apply the same rule in the shared core so
the game and every gym behave identically.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — add the per-upgrade temporary-window TTL to the
  catalogue (`PowerUpEntry`) with per-kind values for the seven instant kinds.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — temporary-stack expiry contract; ensure a
  permanent grant cannot strand a temporary stack.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — start/expire a window for the seven instant
  kinds using the catalogue TTL; keep `_expireTimedEffect` clearing the
  temporary level; capture resolved stats for any queued one-shot pulse.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — clear (or bind) `_tempWeaponStacks` in the
  permanent `equipWeapon` branch; source the weapon TTL per definition.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — existing `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` becomes the default
  weapon TTL (no behaviour change).
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — occupancy follows the temporary stack's expiry
  (no change expected beyond the store behaviour).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — effective-level/countdown/`∞` correctness for the newly
  windowed kinds.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots*.test.ts`,
  `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` — regression tests per kind.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.2/§4.4.3 — replace the "no temporary
  window" exception with the per-upgrade TTL rule.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — queued one-shot effects.** Bomb/Smart Bomb/Strike queue a pulse that
  fires later; if the level reverts before the pulse resolves, the pulse must
  still use the level resolved at pickup. Mitigation: capture the resolved
  stats at pickup (the TTL window makes this rare, but the pulse must not read
  a reverted store).
- **Risk — TTL values are balance tuning.** The proposed instant-kind TTLs
  (10 s / 15 s) are conservative starting points; they live in the catalogue so
  the producer can retune without code changes.
- **Risk — HUD expectations.** A field-pickup window for a one-shot kind may
  be invisible today (no row); the row stays keyed to permanent ownership, so
  the level still reverts without adding a new HUD row.
- **Risk — gym↔game divergence.** Fixing only `PlayScene` would break parity;
  the change belongs in the shared core and the existing guards enforce it.
- **Risk — level-scaled TTL interaction.** For timed kinds the TTL is the
  level-resolved effect duration; a level-up mid-window extends the current
  window to the new duration (existing refresh semantics) and must not create a
  second, competing timer.
- **Scope-creep risk.** The neighbouring "upgrade power" tuning (e.g.
  AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T) and the distinct-consumable-type redesign
  (AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN) must not be pulled in; this item only restores the
  temporary-revert contract.
- **Assumption.** The seven instant kinds are exactly those confirmed above by
  reproduction; the timed kinds and weapons need no behaviour change beyond
  AC3.
- **Assumption.** Consumables already granted persist and never time out
  (producer Q2 answer).

## Related work

- **AH-0MUX802450085VZZ** — Field power-up/weapon pickups must upgrade the item
  TEMPORARILY, not permanently (completed). Introduced the split and its
  "Resolved decision 4: no temporary window" exception that this item
  supersedes.
- **AH-0MUX9T6YF007NNZC** — F2: Power-up temporary/permanent split
  (completed).
- **AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP** — F3: Weapon temporary/permanent split (completed).
- **AH-0MUX9T7QA008CW73** — F4: Choice and HUD consume permanent/effective
  levels (completed).
- **AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN** — Consider a distinct power-up type for consumable
  temporary grants (completed) — related consumable-persistence decision.
- **AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF** — Limit the number of power-up slots (completed) —
  temporary stacks occupy slots while held.
- **AH-0MVSSSFXK005ZW8O** — Restarted levels do not handle hold full correctly
  (open) — checkpoint/resume may restore the same temporary stacks.
- **AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T** — Weapon upgrades are too powerful (idea) — a
  permanent stack left behind by this bug would compound that concern.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.2/§4.4.3 — the documented
  temporary/permanent split and its untimed exception.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD** – Strength of mini-boss and boss should raise with the fire power of the player (completed)
- **AH-0MVSF6AU40094YOM** – Document the wheel reward and unlock removal (blocked)
- **AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD** – Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (open)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: always, collected, increase, level, owned (+12 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: always, collected, increase, level, owned (+12 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: always, collected, increase, level, owned (+9 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1:** "For the seven kinds with no timed effect (`bomb`, `smart_bomb`,
  `strike`, `phase_shift`, `teleport`, `extra_life`, `mystery_ufo`), what
  expiry should their temporary level use? (a) uniform temporary window,
  (b) immediate one-shot, (c) end of wave/level."
  — Answer (producer, interactive): **(a) each upgrade defines its TTL** —
  every field pickup gets a real expiry, and the window length is a property of
  the upgrade item rather than one global constant. Source: producer reply in
  session `herdr-1793238289-1865546-26173`. Consequence recorded in Resolved
  decision 1 (timed effects keep their level-resolved duration as TTL; instant
  kinds gain a per-catalogue TTL with proposed 10 s / 15 s values).
- **Q2:** "Confirm that consumables already granted by a temporary pickup
  (lives, Phase Shift charges, Teleport uses) persist when the temporary level
  reverts, i.e. only the level reverts."
  — Answer (producer, interactive): **yes — consumables do not have a timer.**
  Source: producer reply in session `herdr-1793238289-1865546-26173`.
- **Q3:** "Is the weapon stale-temporary-stack defect (a field pickup followed
  by a permanent grant leaves the temporary stack forever) in scope for this
  item?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive): **yes.** Source: producer reply in session
  `herdr-1793238289-1865546-26173`. Consequence: AC3 and the
